hyp:logistic_L2_regularization.statement: L2 regularization with proper strength (lambda in [0.0, 0.01, 0.1, 1.0, 10.0]) will improve generalization as measured by 5-fold cross-validated Brier score compared to the unregularized baseline (lambda=0).

hyp:interaction_features.statement: Adding interaction features (x0*x1, x1*x2, x2*x3, x0*x3) to logistic regression with lambda=0.1 will significantly improve Brier score, detectable by paired t-test across 5 folds (t > 2.0).

hyp:model_compression.statement: Moderate sparsity (20-40%) with 4-bit quantization will retain most dense model performance, while extreme sparsity (60%) will suffer significant degradation.

claim:q1_lambda_0p1_best.statement: Among lambda values [0.0, 0.01, 0.1, 1.0, 10.0], lambda=0.1 yields the lowest 5-fold cross-validated Brier score (0.207077), improving by 0.00890 over the unregularized baseline (lambda=0.0, Brier=0.215977).

data.method: 5-fold contiguous block CV with full-batch GD, 200 iters, lr=0.1

claim:q2_interactions_significant.statement: Adding interaction features (x0*x1, x1*x2, x2*x3, x0*x3) to logistic regression with lambda=0.1 significantly improves performance: paired t-test across 5 folds yields t=3.91 (> 2.0 threshold), indicating statistically significant improvement (mean Brier reduction = 0.0257).

claim:q3_compression_best_config.statement: Among 6 compression configurations (sparsity 20/40/60%, quantization 4/8 bits), sparsity20_bits4 retains the most dense-model performance with retention=0.9992 (compressed Brier=0.14187 vs dense Brier=0.14176).
